identity.name: HINDUJA GLOBAL SOLS. LTD.
identity.industry: IT-Enabled Services / Business Process Management (CX-BPM + Digital/AI) + Media (broadband / cable-DTH) conglomerate

summary.oneLiner: HGS is a two-engine Hinduja Group story — a transforming CX-BPM/Digital-AI services business plus a loss-making Media (linear-TV + broadband) arm — that called FY26 a "disciplined transformation / legacy-runoff" year: consolidated revenue was roughly flat at INR 4,307 cr but ~200 bps of margin self-help lifted FY26 EBITDA to INR 649 cr (13.4%), with Q4 (INR 1,085 cr rev, 15.7% EBITDA margin) flagged as the inflection/"trend-shifter". The bull case is a record 79 new client signings, AgentX™/Realized AI moving from pilots to production, and a cash-rich balance sheet (net treasury ~INR 5,346 cr) funding the pivot; the overhang is a deeply negative standalone EPS of INR (34.52), a Media division still bleeding (~INR 175 cr FY26 loss) and a stock trading at ~INR 400 vs ~INR 1,700 book — the market is pricing value destruction until the turnaround proves out.

one-line thesis: HGS is a two-engine Hinduja Group story — a transforming CX-BPM/Digital-AI services business plus a loss-making Media (linear-TV + broadband) arm — that called FY26 a "disciplined transformation / legacy-runoff" year: consolidated revenue was roughly flat at INR 4,307 cr but ~200 bps of margin self-help lifted FY26 EBITDA to INR 649 cr (13.4%), with Q4 (INR 1,085 cr rev, 15.7% EBITDA margin) flagged as the inflection/"trend-shifter". The bull case is a record 79 new client signings, AgentX™/Realized AI moving from pilots to production, and a cash-rich balance sheet (net treasury ~INR 5,346 cr) funding the pivot; the overhang is a deeply negative standalone EPS of INR (34.52), a Media division still bleeding (~INR 175 cr FY26 loss) and a stock trading at ~INR 400 vs ~INR 1,700 book — the market is pricing value destruction until the turnaround proves out.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q4 / FY26 | YoY / QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (consol, ops) | Q4 INR 1,085 cr; FY26 INR 4,307 cr | ~flat YoY | "Modest" growth; reported drag from client ramp-downs/runoffs, said non-recurring |
| Total income | Q4 INR 1,255 cr; FY26 INR 4,857 cr | — | Includes other income (Q4 INR 170 cr; FY26 INR 549.7 cr — large, treasury-driven) |
| EBITDA / margin | Q4 INR 197.1 cr @ 15.7%; FY26 INR 648.6 cr @ 13.4% | margin +~200 bps | Self-help from real-estate/tech/infra cost rationalization; Q4 = sequential recovery |
| PAT / EPS | FY26 standalone earnings INR (160) cr; basic EPS INR (34.52) | negative | Mgmt: "turnaround year"; expects negative EPS to reverse in FY27+ |
| Media segment loss | Q4 ~INR 50 cr loss; FY26 ~INR 175 cr loss | persistent | Linear-TV headwinds; broadband/CelerityX the offset |
| Cash / net treasury | Net treasury & cash surplus ~INR 5,346 cr | strong | Conservative leverage; funds AI + Project Ganga without external capital |
| Dividend | Final INR 5/share (FV INR 10), subject to AGM | resumed | No dividend last year — signal of confidence |
| New client signings | 79 (BPM + Digital) | record ("best year ever") | Most growth comes via existing clients → FY27 revenue base |
> Watch: other income is a large share of total income (treasury on ~INR 5,346 cr surplus) — operating profitability is thinner than headline EBITDA suggests. Standalone vs consolidated framing differs (EPS quoted on standalone INR (160) cr).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue:** No hard number. FY27 = "rebuild year"; "meaningful revenue visibility" from 79 new signings ramping + AI assistants moving pilot→production; expects diversification (Digital/AI) mix to accelerate. "Cautiously optimistic" amid macro/client caution.
- **Margin:** Cost-discipline actions "materializing"; ~200 bps already delivered FY26; some incremental cost still flows through H1 FY27. Targets "steady improvements in growth and margins over time" — no specific exit-margin target.
- **Media / losses:** Aim to narrow Media losses via revenue optimization (CelerityX 2x revenue / 5x TCV) + cost cuts (bandwidth cost 28%→26% of retail rev; broadcaster/G&A negotiations). Declined a firm break-even timeline — promised an update at end of Q2 FY27.
- **Project Ganga:** 2 million households over 2–3 years; up to 10,000 DSP entrepreneurs + 100,000 youth digital-skilling. HGS investment is know-how only (asset-light); capex funded by UP CM Yuva Scheme. Revenue model = ISP. Profit contribution "kickers" hoped for, not quantified.
- **Capital allocation:** Dividend resumed; reinvesting cost-savings into sales capacity, offerings, AI CoEs.
order book & pipeline:
- Not an order-book business; KPI proxies: 79 new logos in FY26 (record); pipeline described as larger, more outcome-led, more integrated/multi-tower.
- AgentX™ at scale: 23 active customers, 21 AI assistants in production (not pilots). Package solutions: 8 live (AMLens, LoanFlow, KYCVision among them). Realized AI "90-day zero-to-production" model.
- Media pipeline: CelerityX enterprise (2x revenue, 5x TCV YoY); Project Ganga MoU (signed 9-Mar) + UP Digital-Skilling MoU.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Revenue by source (FY26):** Core CX-BPM 55% / Digital & Media services 45% (Q4: 58% / 42%). Mix shifting toward higher-margin digital.
- **By vertical (FY26):** Tech-Media-Telecom 50%, BFSI 18%, Retail 17%, Public sector 8% (public-sector anchored by UK + Canada wins + Project Ganga).
- **By origination (where sold):** India 38%, US 28%, UK 13%, others ~5% (plus Europe/APAC).
- **By delivery:** India 42% (highest), US 19%, Philippines ~13%, UK 10% (US+Canada+UK ~28% combined for regulated/hi-tech onshore work).
- **Media:** Retail broadband (ONEOTT/OIL) + CelerityX enterprise = "engines of forward growth"; Digital-TV (cable/DTH) in managed decline — churn held <2% (Q4 ~0.62% vs 2–3% industry), ARPU stable at INR 122. Broadband value-migration: >100 Mbps users 10.7%→15% YoY; entry (≤50 Mbps) base 54%→46%.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Agentic AI / Realized AI:** flagship narrative — "AI itself no longer a differentiator, execution is"; FDE-led delivery, multi-agent workforce with human oversight; AgentX™ Workbench accelerators.
- **Package solutions (productized IP):** AMLens (AML), LoanFlow, KYCVision, DaVinci™ (CX data-lake) — faster deployment, higher-margin, repeatable.
- **Public sector:** UK adult-social-care "Case Assist" (4 hrs → 30 min per case) now scaling to multiple UK/Canada agencies, early US interest.
- **Broadband / CelerityX:** retail upsell to higher bandwidth + enterprise connectivity growth; Project Ganga as asset-light rural-broadband expansion.
- **~18,000 employees** as the "practitioner" moat layered with AI.
margins & cost dynamics:
- ~200 bps EBITDA margin improvement from real-estate, technology and infrastructure rationalization — described as structural, with more cost flowing through into H1 FY27.
- Margin mix: Digital/AI/package solutions and onshore regulated work carry higher margins on a "resilient core" of CX-BPM.
- Media: bandwidth cost (key input for broadband) cut 28%→26% of retail revenue via telco negotiation/utilization; DTV content cost reduced via broadcaster negotiation; G&A cuts.
- Heavy reliance on offshore India delivery (42%) as a structural cost advantage.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Capital deployed in AI-led centers of excellence, package solutions, and broadband/CelerityX build-out — funded internally; conservative leverage maintained.
- Project Ganga is deliberately asset-light for HGS (capex via CM Yuva Scheme loans to DSPs) — HGS contributes expertise/training and earns via ISP model.
- No large announced greenfield capex; investment is in capability + sales capacity, not physical plant.
capital allocation:
- Dividend resumed: INR 5/share final (none last year) — signalling return-to-profit confidence.
- Net treasury/cash surplus ~INR 5,346 cr; mgmt explicitly "not concerned about shortage of funds" — funds transformation internally.
- An investor pointedly pushed for RoCE focus (book value ~INR 1,700/share vs price ~INR 400) — mgmt acknowledged and said "we will look into that." Capital efficiency is the key external ask.
risks & watch-items:
- **Standalone EPS INR (34.52)** / standalone loss INR (160) cr — company is loss-making at the bottom line; turnaround unproven.
- **Media (NXTDIGITAL) losses** ~INR 175 cr FY26 — linear-TV (cable/DTH) in secular decline; broadband recovery "happening, but not at a rapid pace"; no break-even timeline given (deferred to Q2 FY27).
- **Client concentration / ramp-downs** drove flat revenue; "runoffs" claimed non-recurring but reduce near-term base.
- **GAAR / income-tax dispute** on NXTDIGITAL merger sub-judice at Bombay HC (hearing 12-Jun-2026) — contingent liability overhang.
- **Other-income dependence:** large treasury other income flatters total income vs operating profitability.
- **Valuation/market skepticism:** price ~INR 400 vs book ~INR 1,700 — market pricing value destruction.
- **Macro / client caution** in near-term IT-services demand; AI commoditization pressure on pricing.
- **Project Ganga execution risk:** large social project, monetization to HGS unquantified.
management quality / tone: - Three-voice call (CEO/Media-WTD/CFO) — coherent "disciplined transformation / legacy runoff / rebuild FY27" framing; consistent and candid on both the BPM turnaround and Media pain. CFO explicitly called FY26 a "turnaround year" and owned the negative EPS. Vyns was straight on linear-TV headwinds ("rather than sitting on our hands and moaning") and honest that broadband recovery is "not at a rapid pace." Somewhat narrative/buzzword-heavy on AI ("Realized AI," "intelligent experience with certainty"). Notably engaged constructively with a retail investor's blunt RoCE/value-destruction critique. Resumed dividend is a credible confidence signal given prior-year omission.
non-obvious takeaways:
- This is effectively a sum-of-parts: a recovering, cash-generative CX-BPM/Digital business subsidizing a structurally challenged Media arm — the equity re-rates only if Media losses shrink or the segment is restructured/separated.
- Net treasury (~INR 5,346 cr) dwarfs the ~INR 400 share price's implied market value relative to book (~INR 1,700) — the bear read is the cash/assets aren't earning their keep (the RoCE critique); the bull read is optionality/asset backing.
- AgentX™ at 23 customers / 21 assistants in production is the most concrete proof-point that the AI story is past pilots — the FY27 thesis hinges on these ramping and the 79 new logos converting.
- Project Ganga is structured to be cash-neutral for HGS (government-funded capex, ISP revenue model) — a low-risk way to scale rural broadband subscribers if execution lands.
- "Other income" doing heavy lifting in total income is the quiet caveat behind the 13.4% EBITDA headline.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

identity.name: HINDUJA GLOBAL SOLS. LTD.
identity.industry: IT-Enabled Services / Business Process Management (CX-BPM + Digital/AI) + Media (broadband / cable-DTH) conglomerate

hero.oneLiner: HGS is a two-engine Hinduja Group story — a transforming CX-BPM/Digital-AI services business plus a loss-making Media (linear-TV + broadband) arm — that called FY26 a "disciplined transformation / legacy-runoff" year: consolidated revenue was roughly flat at INR 4,307 cr but ~200 bps of margin self-help lifted FY26 EBITDA to INR 649 cr (13.4%), with Q4 (INR 1,085 cr rev, 15.7% EBITDA margin) flagged as the inflection/"trend-shifter". The bull case is a record 79 new client signings, AgentX™/Realized AI moving from pilots to production, and a cash-rich balance sheet (net treasury ~INR 5,346 cr) funding the pivot; the overhang is a deeply negative standalone EPS of INR (34.52), a Media division still bleeding (~INR 175 cr FY26 loss) and a stock trading at ~INR 400 vs ~INR 1,700 book — the market is pricing value destruction until the turnaround proves out.
hero.industry: IT-Enabled Services / Business Process Management (CX-BPM + Digital/AI) + Media (broadband / cable-DTH) conglomerate

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Introduced a sharper market position as the Intelligent Experiences partner in end-March 2026", with the portfolio "realigned ... around Intelligent Interactions, Operations and Platforms".
- Frames the market shift as "Enterprises are moving from AI pilots to AI execution", where "Buyers are prioritizing speed-to-value, governance and scalability" and "Success increasingly depends on delivering business impact, not just deploying AI".
- Claims the relevant demand is for "partners who can combine technology, operations and execution", with opportunities "aligned to HGS' strategic strengths, including AI-led transformation, platform services and intelligent operations".
- Digital media arm positions on the "3A's, Artificial Intelligence, Analytics & Automation to build out an integrated connectivity mesh across the country", spanning terrestrial platforms with SDWAN layered to broadband-over-satellite.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Revenue by source (FY26):** Core CX-BPM 55% / Digital & Media services 45% (Q4: 58% / 42%). Mix shifting toward higher-margin digital.
- **By vertical (FY26):** Tech-Media-Telecom 50%, BFSI 18%, Retail 17%, Public sector 8% (public-sector anchored by UK + Canada wins + Project Ganga).
- **By origination (where sold):** India 38%, US 28%, UK 13%, others ~5% (plus Europe/APAC).
- **By delivery:** India 42% (highest), US 19%, Philippines ~13%, UK 10% (US+Canada+UK ~28% combined for regulated/hi-tech onshore work).
- **Media:** Retail broadband (ONEOTT/OIL) + CelerityX enterprise = "engines of forward growth"; Digital-TV (cable/DTH) in managed decline — churn held <2% (Q4 ~0.62% vs 2–3% industry), ARPU stable at INR 122. Broadband value-migration: >100 Mbps users 10.7%→15% YoY; entry (≤50 Mbps) base 54%→46%.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Not an order-book business; KPI proxies: 79 new logos in FY26 (record); pipeline described as larger, more outcome-led, more integrated/multi-tower.
- AgentX™ at scale: 23 active customers, 21 AI assistants in production (not pilots). Package solutions: 8 live (AMLens, LoanFlow, KYCVision among them). Realized AI "90-day zero-to-production" model.
- Media pipeline: CelerityX enterprise (2x revenue, 5x TCV YoY); Project Ganga MoU (signed 9-Mar) + UP Digital-Skilling MoU.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue:** No hard number. FY27 = "rebuild year"; "meaningful revenue visibility" from 79 new signings ramping + AI assistants moving pilot→production; expects diversification (Digital/AI) mix to accelerate. "Cautiously optimistic" amid macro/client caution.
- **Margin:** Cost-discipline actions "materializing"; ~200 bps already delivered FY26; some incremental cost still flows through H1 FY27. Targets "steady improvements in growth and margins over time" — no specific exit-margin target.
- **Media / losses:** Aim to narrow Media losses via revenue optimization (CelerityX 2x revenue / 5x TCV) + cost cuts (bandwidth cost 28%→26% of retail rev; broadcaster/G&A negotiations). Declined a firm break-even timeline — promised an update at end of Q2 FY27.
- **Project Ganga:** 2 million households over 2–3 years; up to 10,000 DSP entrepreneurs + 100,000 youth digital-skilling. HGS investment is know-how only (asset-light); capex funded by UP CM Yuva Scheme. Revenue model = ISP. Profit contribution "kickers" hoped for, not quantified.
- **Capital allocation:** Dividend resumed; reinvesting cost-savings into sales capacity, offerings, AI CoEs.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Agentic AI / Realized AI:** flagship narrative — "AI itself no longer a differentiator, execution is"; FDE-led delivery, multi-agent workforce with human oversight; AgentX™ Workbench accelerators.
- **Package solutions (productized IP):** AMLens (AML), LoanFlow, KYCVision, DaVinci™ (CX data-lake) — faster deployment, higher-margin, repeatable.
- **Public sector:** UK adult-social-care "Case Assist" (4 hrs → 30 min per case) now scaling to multiple UK/Canada agencies, early US interest.
- **Broadband / CelerityX:** retail upsell to higher bandwidth + enterprise connectivity growth; Project Ganga as asset-light rural-broadband expansion.
- **~18,000 employees** as the "practitioner" moat layered with AI.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- ~200 bps EBITDA margin improvement from real-estate, technology and infrastructure rationalization — described as structural, with more cost flowing through into H1 FY27.
- Margin mix: Digital/AI/package solutions and onshore regulated work carry higher margins on a "resilient core" of CX-BPM.
- Media: bandwidth cost (key input for broadband) cut 28%→26% of retail revenue via telco negotiation/utilization; DTV content cost reduced via broadcaster negotiation; G&A cuts.
- Heavy reliance on offshore India delivery (42%) as a structural cost advantage.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Dividend resumed: INR 5/share final (none last year) — signalling return-to-profit confidence.
- Net treasury/cash surplus ~INR 5,346 cr; mgmt explicitly "not concerned about shortage of funds" — funds transformation internally.
- An investor pointedly pushed for RoCE focus (book value ~INR 1,700/share vs price ~INR 400) — mgmt acknowledged and said "we will look into that." Capital efficiency is the key external ask.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - Three-voice call (CEO/Media-WTD/CFO) — coherent "disciplined transformation / legacy runoff / rebuild FY27" framing; consistent and candid on both the BPM turnaround and Media pain. CFO explicitly called FY26 a "turnaround year" and owned the negative EPS. Vyns was straight on linear-TV headwinds ("rather than sitting on our hands and moaning") and honest that broadband recovery is "not at a rapid pace." Somewhat narrative/buzzword-heavy on AI ("Realized AI," "intelligent experience with certainty"). Notably engaged constructively with a retail investor's blunt RoCE/value-destruction critique. Resumed dividend is a credible confidence signal given prior-year omission.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Standalone EPS INR (34.52)** / standalone loss INR (160) cr — company is loss-making at the bottom line; turnaround unproven.
- **Media (NXTDIGITAL) losses** ~INR 175 cr FY26 — linear-TV (cable/DTH) in secular decline; broadband recovery "happening, but not at a rapid pace"; no break-even timeline given (deferred to Q2 FY27).
- **Client concentration / ramp-downs** drove flat revenue; "runoffs" claimed non-recurring but reduce near-term base.
- **GAAR / income-tax dispute** on NXTDIGITAL merger sub-judice at Bombay HC (hearing 12-Jun-2026) — contingent liability overhang.
- **Other-income dependence:** large treasury other income flatters total income vs operating profitability.
- **Valuation/market skepticism:** price ~INR 400 vs book ~INR 1,700 — market pricing value destruction.
- **Macro / client caution** in near-term IT-services demand; AI commoditization pressure on pricing.
- **Project Ganga execution risk:** large social project, monetization to HGS unquantified.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- This is effectively a sum-of-parts: a recovering, cash-generative CX-BPM/Digital business subsidizing a structurally challenged Media arm — the equity re-rates only if Media losses shrink or the segment is restructured/separated.
- Net treasury (~INR 5,346 cr) dwarfs the ~INR 400 share price's implied market value relative to book (~INR 1,700) — the bear read is the cash/assets aren't earning their keep (the RoCE critique); the bull read is optionality/asset backing.
- AgentX™ at 23 customers / 21 assistants in production is the most concrete proof-point that the AI story is past pilots — the FY27 thesis hinges on these ramping and the 79 new logos converting.
- Project Ganga is structured to be cash-neutral for HGS (government-funded capex, ISP revenue model) — a low-risk way to scale rural broadband subscribers if execution lands.
- "Other income" doing heavy lifting in total income is the quiet caveat behind the 13.4% EBITDA headline.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Consol rev INR 1,085 cr (Q4) / INR 4,307 cr (FY); EBITDA 15.7% (Q4) / 13.4% (FY), +~200 bps from cost self-help; standalone EPS INR (34.52); Media loss ~INR 50 cr (Q4) / ~INR 175 cr (FY); 79 new logos (record); dividend INR 5/sh resumed; net treasury ~INR 5,346 cr; AgentX™ 23 customers / 21 assistants live; Project Ganga + UP digital-skilling MoUs signed (Mar); GAAR appeal at Bombay HC (hearing 12-Jun-26).
- _Next Q (Q1/Q2 FY27) → check: (1) does the 79-logo cohort ramp into revenue growth? (2) Media loss trajectory + the promised end-Q2 break-even/timeline update; (3) margin holding/expanding as H1 incremental costs flow through; (4) standalone EPS turning toward positive; (5) Project Ganga DSP/household traction + any revenue; (6) GAAR/Bombay HC outcome; (7) CelerityX revenue/TCV momentum; (8) RoCE/capital-efficiency response to investor pressure._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Awards] "Continued recognition for our innovative capabilities and people practices - Banking Tech Awards, GPTW"; separately, ONEOTT iNTERTAINMENT Ltd. (OIL) was "conferred with the prestigious 'Best Future Ready Network of the Year 2025-26' at the 12th BCS Ratna Awards", citing "consistent innovation in technology and leveraging its vast partner-driven network".
- [Case study] A beverage can manufacturer engagement (Manufacturing; Data & Analytics on Microsoft Azure and PowerBI) is credited with "99% accuracy in reducing variance between planned and actual sales data", "80% improvement in account receivables, optimizing inventory costs by 70%" and "95% accuracy in production planning ensured, resulting in a 15% reduction in production costs" — client-reported outcomes, not HGS financials.
- [Structure] The business is presented under two named leaders — Venkatesh Korla (Global CEO) for the services business and Vynsley Fernandes (Whole-time Director, HGS & CEO, NXTDIGITAL Media Business) for digital media, with Mahesh Kumar Nutalapati as Global CFO.
